page: OVHcloud b2-15 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for balanced compute and memory operations. Hosted on a KVM hypervisor, it features 4 dedicated physical cores mapped to 4 vCPUs using Intel x86_64 Haswell architecture at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz without hyper-threading. The system includes 15 GB of RAM, yielding 3.75 GB per core, accompanied by 32 KB L1d, 4 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. Storage consists of a bundled 100 GB local SSD volume. No hardware GPU acceleration is included, and public networking features a baseline rate of 0 Gbps without complimentary IPv4 addresses.

Synthetic benchmark performance reflects the aging Haswell instruction core. Stress-ng scores show 959.69 in single-core and 3669.99 in multi-core metrics, positioning the processor in the lower percentile ranges. Geekbench evaluations yield 1066.0 for single-core and 3132.0 for multi-core workflows. Instruction extensions are restricted to AVX and FMA, lacking modern AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets, which diminishes throughput in modern machine learning tasks such as medium 7B model inference (yielding 10.43 prompt tokens per second). Memory benchmarks demonstrate 347.69 GB/s for small cached reads, tapering to 37.17 GB/s for uncached reads and 22.32 GB/s for writes.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the b2-15 offers dedicated CPU capacity rather than shared or burstable cores, ensuring predictable performance for continuous baseline operations. However, computational throughput per core remains modest due to the 2.0 GHz clock and generational architectural limits. The bundled local SSD and 15 GB memory pool make the instance practical for cost-conscious environments that prioritize predictable RAM and local disk over intensive raw computation. Suitable workloads include staging or testing environments, low-throughput databases, internal tooling, lightweight CI/CD pipeline steps, and static web serving.
description: OVHcloud b2-15 is a general-purpose cloud virtual machine powered by 4 dedicated Intel Haswell x86_64 cores operating at 2.0 GHz, paired with 15 GB of RAM and 100 GB of local SSD storage. The configuration lacks discrete GPU hardware and provides a 1:3.75 core-to-memory ratio across a KVM hypervisor. Benchmark assessments place single-core performance at 959.69 in stress-ng and 1066.0 in Geekbench, reflecting the older Haswell CPU architecture. Uncached memory throughput measures 37.17 GB/s for reads and 22.32 GB/s for writes, matching lower-tier throughput tiers. The instance delivers steady execution without burst credits due to dedicated core mapping, yet exhibits weak overall compute and multi-threading capabilities. PassMark database tests achieve average ratings, while Redis throughput attains 5.93 million operations per second. The b2-15 provides balanced resources for cost-sensitive scenarios, making it suitable for staging servers, modest database instances, lightweight background worker services, and low-traffic web serving.
